summary: Defined the task-level hardening architecture for SDK-native system/user role separation, combined request-size enforcement, one-call/no-tools preservation, a Python 3.12 hash-locked dependency graph, and one fail-closed dependency-audit gate shared by local verification and CI, without changing the API, product scope, data boundary, frontend, or database.
decisions: HARDEN-001 changes only the existing Gemini adapter plus repository dependency and CI verification controls. The FastAPI endpoint, Pydantic response, deterministic rules, source dataset, runtime provider, local-only deployment posture, and candidate-only human-authority boundary remain unchanged.

The fixed project-owned SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION remains a non-interpolated constant and is supplied only through GenerateContentConfig.system_instruction. User contents contains only the fixed SUPPLIED_SYNTHETIC_DATA_JSON label plus the canonically serialized minimized payload; the policy is never duplicated in user content and untrusted payload strings never enter the system role.

The existing 128 KiB request-input ceiling is evaluated before generate_content as the sum of the exact UTF-8 bytes of the system instruction and user content. Exceeding it makes zero provider calls and returns the existing sanitized configuration_error model fallback, preserving deterministic API output.

The SDK call retains the existing JSON MIME type and Pydantic-owned response schema, 2,048 output-token ceiling, thinking-disabled configuration, 30-second client timeout, 64 KiB response boundary, evidence-reference allowlist, sanitized error mapping, and exactly zero or one invocation. No tools, retry, repair call, fallback model, side effect, or extra data source may be added.

Fake-client tests inspect the actual generate_content call rather than inferred output. They prove exact system_instruction ownership, user-content labeling and JSON containment, instruction-like synthetic strings remaining in the user role, fixed policy absence from user content, private environment sentinel absence from both roles, no tools key, and zero calls for a combined over-limit input.

requirements-agent.txt remains the human-reviewed direct dependency input and continues to include backend/requirements.txt. The selected dependency-audit tool is added there with an exact == pin; ranged agentic direct constraints may remain review inputs because the generated lock resolves every installed package exactly.

One repository-root requirements.lock is generated from requirements-agent.txt in a clean Python 3.12 environment with a documented exact lock-compiler version and SHA-256 hash generation. It contains the complete application, test, agentic, and audit transitive graph, uses exact versions and artifact hashes for every installable requirement, and is regenerated rather than manually edited.

All GitHub Actions workflows that install the Python application or agentic tooling install exclusively with python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock. requirements-agent.txt is no longer a CI installation source; it remains the direct-review and lock-regeneration input.

The dependency audit is declared in .ai/project.json as a required security check against requirements.lock with strict collection errors, hash enforcement, no dependency re-resolution where supported by the pinned tool, and no ignored vulnerability IDs. Normal agentctl verification and --security-only therefore execute the same fail-closed audit without application credentials or live Vertex AI access.

Verification evidence must cover direct-manifest/lock consistency, exact transitive pins and SHA-256 hashes, a clean Python 3.12 pip --require-hashes installation, pip check, the required dependency audit, backend and agentic tests, secret baseline, OpenAPI validation, and source-dataset immutability. Known applicable advisories block until dependencies are updated and the lock regenerated, unless a separate approved exception records applicability, controls, owner, and expiry.

Infrastructure impact is true because .github/workflows/** and the operational .ai/project.json security checks change. This does not enable or deploy application infrastructure and introduces no runtime service; database and frontend impacts are false.
Contract change is false. contracts/openapi.yaml remains authoritative and must validate byte-for-byte unchanged because request and response behavior are preserved.

No ADR or project-wide SYSTEM.md change is required: ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0003's active replacement decision, and ADR-0004 already authorize and constrain the human, synthetic-data, local-backend, and direct one-call Vertex AI boundaries. This task closes implementation and supply-chain gaps inside those accepted decisions.

risks.description: A partial prompt refactor could still duplicate policy into user content, promote untrusted FHIR-derived text to the system role, or accidentally send private runtime configuration.
risks.mitigation: Construct two explicit fixed-role values, prohibit runtime interpolation in the system instruction, keep user content to a label plus canonical JSON, and assert the exact fake-client arguments with adversarial instruction-like data and environment sentinels.

risks.description: Moving text between SDK fields could weaken the 128 KiB guard or allow an oversized request to reach the provider.
risks.mitigation: Measure the sum of both exact UTF-8 role payloads before invocation, preserve the existing sanitized fallback status, and independently test boundary and over-boundary values with provider call count fixed at zero when exceeded.

risks.description: A dependency audit that resolves a different graph, silently ignores advisories, or treats collection/network errors as success could provide false assurance.
risks.mitigation: Audit the committed hashed lock with the exact-pinned audit tool, strict/hash-enforced fail-closed flags, no ignore IDs, and the identical required project security command in local verification and CI.

risks.description: The direct manifests and generated lock could drift, leaving reviewed intent different from what CI installs.
risks.mitigation: Document one clean Python 3.12 regeneration command using an exact compiler version, prohibit hand edits, add direct-input/lock consistency evidence, and make every workflow install only the hash-locked graph.

risks.description: A lock generated under a different Python or platform assumption may fail on the supported Ubuntu/Python 3.12 CI environment despite containing hashes.
risks.mitigation: Generate and verify for Python 3.12, include valid SHA-256 artifacts for the resolved graph, and require a clean Ubuntu-compatible pip --require-hashes installation plus pip check before acceptance.

risks.description: Hash pinning can be mistaken for proof that dependencies are trustworthy or vulnerability-free.
risks.mitigation: Keep artifact integrity, advisory audit, direct-dependency review, tests, and security review as separate controls; resolve audit findings explicitly and retain the feature's statement that hashes do not replace source review.

risks.description: Adding the audit package to the unified lock increases the tooling dependency graph and the audit may report on itself.
risks.mitigation: Keep the audit tool exactly pinned as an intentional direct tooling dependency, include its graph in the same lock, and treat applicable findings in tooling with the same update-or-approved-exception policy.

notes_for_next_agent: Orchestrator: contract_change is false; validate contracts/openapi.yaml unchanged and do not start contract, database, or frontend work. Start backend, infrastructure/tooling within the backend role's allowed paths, and independent testing because those impacts are true.

Backend owner: limit production behavior changes to backend/app/gemini.py. Preserve all public/model failure statuses and constraints, compute the combined role-byte limit before the call, and pass the fixed policy only through GenerateContentConfig.system_instruction.

Backend owner: update requirements-agent.txt, generate requirements.lock under Python 3.12 with hashes using the documented exact compiler version, change all Python-installing workflows to --require-hashes, and add one required strict audit command to .ai/project.json. Do not add ignored advisory IDs.

Backend owner: add focused fake-client and dependency-consistency tests under tests/backend/**, run a clean hash-enforced install and pip check, and record exact commands and selected audit/compiler versions in backend-report.json.

Tester: independently verify role separation using adversarial instruction-like data, no private environment sentinels in either role, no tools, combined-limit zero-call behavior, one-call/failure invariants, direct-input/lock consistency, every exact pin/hash, clean Python 3.12 installation, and audit failure behavior without credentials.

Security/reviewer: confirm no OpenAPI, dataset, deterministic rule, frontend, database, provider authority, retry/tool, credential, deployment, or product-scope expansion; assess both the exact SDK request arguments and the exact locked/audited graph.
